segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 50% YoY on strong demand for Arm technology and several large deals. Licensing today is a leading indicator of royalty revenue tomorrow.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 8% YoY, helped by higher royalty rates on newer designs such as Armv9 and by data center royalties doubling, partly offset by memory pricing pressure on smartphones.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new processors and platform technology; the GAAP figure includes $267M of share-based pay (paying staff in shares).

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $101M of share-based pay.

oneTimers: Share-based pay is the main gap between the two profit numbers: the non-GAAP reconciliation adds back $377M of equity-settled share-based compensation (plus $48M of related employer taxes, net, and $12M of acquisition-related expenses), which is why GAAP net income of $130M sits far below non-GAAP net income of $566M.

The year-ago quarter included a $131M gain on selling a business, inside its $128M of other non-operating income — this quarter had no such gain, which is a big reason GAAP net income fell 45% YoY even as revenue rose 27%.

sources.label: Official earnings release — shareholder letter, Form 6-K Exhibit 99.2 (SEC EDGAR)

verdict: Arm's revenue hit a record $1.44B, up 27%, as licensing jumped 50% — but heavy share-based pay held GAAP profit to $130M, less than a quarter of the non-GAAP figure.
otherDetail: Combined net other income was $7M: interest income of $29M, less $2M of other non-operating expense (together the $27M shown as otherIncomeM), less a $20M loss from equity investments (the separate equityM line).
footerNote: Arm calls its direct cost 'cost of sales' ($42M) and reports just two revenue lines: license and other, and royalty.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: non-GAAP, down 73% YoY; operating cash flow was $207M

takeaways.title: Licensing is doing the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: License and other revenue jumped 50% to $773M — 54% of all revenue — as customers paid up for newer Arm technology. Those designs enter production later, so today's licensing surge points to future royalty growth.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit is much smaller than it looks
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.12, down from $0.22 a year ago, while non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.52. The gap is mostly $377M of share-based pay counted under GAAP — and last year's GAAP figure was flattered by a $131M gain on selling a business.

takeaways.title: Next quarter is guided higher
takeaways.text: Arm guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $1.54B (plus or minus $50M) with non-GAAP EPS of $0.56 (plus or minus $0.04). Data center royalties already doubled this quarter as Arm-based server chips spread through the big cloud providers.
